name: marine_propeller
description: 4-blade marine propeller (aluminium bronze / 6061) — cylindrical hub with shaft through-bore and 4 twisted, skewed hydrofoil blades; radial_peaks=4 + bore/envelope gates plus thrust & torque FEM.

stages.prompt:
4-blade marine propeller, parametric.

Frame: hub axis along Z, bottom face on the XY plane (z = 0), centred in X and Y. mm.
- Overall bounding box exactly 120 (X) x 120 (Y) x 24 (Z): z = 0..24.
- Central cylindrical hub: outer dia 28 (r = 14), height 24 (z = 0..24).
- Concentric through-bore dia 10 (r = 5) along Z through (0,0), open on both z = 0 and z = 24; the cut must span the full hub height — use a bore cylinder centred at (0,0,12) with height ~30 so it clears both faces (a centred tool shifted to z = -1 leaves the top half solid).
- 4 identical twisted hydrofoil blades spaced 0/90/180/270 deg around Z:
  * Each blade runs radially from r = 8 (root station 6 mm inside the r = 14 hub wall — a fat union overlap; still 3 mm clear of the r = 5 bore) out to tip radius r = 60 (propeller dia 120 — bound the tip to the r = 60 cylinder).
  * Loft each blade across >= 3 radial stations (e.g. r = 8, 35, 60) using thin hydrofoil/elliptical sections: chord ~18-22 mm, max thickness ~3.0-3.5 mm, with progressive helicoidal pitch twist (~32 deg at the root to ~18 deg at the tip).
  * Keep ALL blade geometry strictly inside z = 2..22 so the flat hub faces define the exact z = 0..24 height.
- Union the 4 blades with the hub, then cut the dia-10 centre through-bore. Blades are SOLID bodies — do not cut slots, channels, weight pockets or voids into them. No fillets, no chamfers; the result must be a single watertight solid.
